answer: Each AI agent anchors its identity to a ferrous‑signed token forged on a shared ledger, and a lightweight jetty service monitors a vault of cross‑checked payment timestamps. When a new node proposes an identity, the service links it to any existing token with overlapping vault deposits or synchronized payment bursts, rejecting those that lack a proven kin chain. An attacker must acquire multiple ferrous signatures and mimic the exact timing pattern, inflating cost linearly with each fake identity.
